description: Glance board for user-facing feature health. A 99% color is used only where the denominator is something that should have worked for the user and success means they got it. Pendant sockets, finalization-job success, blended gateway requests, and cloud push-to-talk are shown without that bar: those numbers are not 'the user got the result'. Drill-down rows ship collapsed so the first paint stays inside the 30s monitor proxy budget. Daily recaps are generation in the last 3 hours, not delivery, and ignore the time picker. Sync histograms reach Conversation shape only after backend-sync joins the Cloud Run exporter; that row uses Cloud Logging of omi_sync_intake meanwhile.

panels.description: Not a user outcome. Share of accepted pendant listen sockets that delivered at least one audio byte. The rest closed before any audio (reconnects). Same rate on iOS and Android. Do not chase 99% here. A user who was not sending audio did not fail to get a recording.
panels.title: Pendant sockets that sent audio

panels.description: Share of sockets that had audio and were not closed by a projection-queue wait or an application error. This is the live session dying while the user was capturing. It is not proof the recording was lost: an unacknowledged tail is closed 1011 on purpose so the client can replay it. Control-only sockets (no audio frames) are excluded. Empty means no audio-bearing closes.
panels.title: Live audio session kept

panels.description: Not 'the user got the recording'. Success / (success + failure) of the finalization job. A failure dead-letters the job and still writes the conversation completed and visible; the summary may be missing and marked retryable. Do not add the dead-letter gauge to this rate: the same event increments both. Stale is fences and discards, not a lost recording. This panel measures live finalization on job=pusher-metrics only; sync on cloud-run-application-metrics is excluded. The two emitters are not deduplicated and must not be blended into a unique-finalization rate. A seconds-scale median with a tens-of-minutes tail is a tail delay, not the typical case.
panels.title: Finalization job succeeded

panels.description: Not what the user received, and not the dashboard time range. Generated / (generated + failed) in the last 3 hours. Failed excludes DailySummaryDeliveryError: the recap was generated and the push did not land. A phone that never registered a token cannot be delivered to. Green at 98%, red under 90%. Reads 'no recaps due' when nobody needed a recap.

Oldest queued or leased finalization job: system-owned work only. Jobs waiting for user BYOK reconnect have a separate informational age gauge and do not page. Replicated per process; aggregate with max(). blocked_byok is excluded by the summary producer; user-side credential waits are not system-caused age. Read it with Queued: a low queue with a steadily climbing age is one stuck job or a few, while a growing queue is a backlog.
panels.title: Oldest job

panels.description: New durable dead-letter jobs over the selected range, estimated from the change in the global Firestore projection (max across replicas before delta, sampled each minute). This survives pod restarts and includes events before a new pod is first scraped, unlike the per-process counter. The projection generation starts 2026-07-25; older jobs are not backfilled. Includes exhausted retries and abandoned BYOK credential waits. Dead-letter jobs are not a count of lost conversations: some already finalized inline, and BYOK abandonment preserves the conversation. Delta extrapolates range edges; short ranges or missing summary samples can be blank. A telemetry gap is not zero. A missing current summary or no successful summary in 15 minutes suppresses the stat.
panels.title: Dead letters

panels.description: Recorded stale capture_finalization terminals in the last 3 hours: count and percentage of all capture terminal events recorded in those 3 hours (success, failure, cancelled and stale). Stale includes deliberate discard, account-cutover and newer-lifecycle fences; it does not establish a missing conversation outcome or lost capture. These events are excluded from the Voice capture success-rate denominator. This is a terminal-event window, not a cohort of captures started in the window or an accepted-minus-terminal backlog. No samples in the window stays blank; this historical window does not prove current reporter health. Live finalization only (job=pusher-metrics), matching the headline; Cloud Run sync events are excluded.
panels.title: Capture stale (3h)

panels.description: Non-zero means the pusher breaker has tripped. A blank panel means no replica published this series at all: that is "the reporter is gone", not "the value is zero", and the two must never render the same.
panels.title: Pusher breaker

panels.description: 1 when the gateway has tripped its breaker; requests are being shed. A blank panel means no replica published this series at all: that is "the reporter is gone", not "the value is zero", and the two must never render the same.
panels.title: AI circuit

panels.description: How many of the three journeys emitted anything in the dashboard's selected time range. A journey that stops reporting looks identical to a journey with no failures, which is the failure mode omi-journey-signal-dead exists to catch. Owner-scoped: chat_response on cloud-run-application-metrics; pusher_session on pusher-metrics; live capture_finalization is accepted by backend-listen-metrics and settled by pusher-metrics, so its accepted counter is read from backend-listen. Cloud Run sync finalization is excluded; these are event windows, not unique captures.

targets.expr: count(count by (journey) ((increase(omi_journey_accepted_total{job="cloud-run-application-metrics",journey="chat_response"}[$__range]) or increase(omi_journey_accepted_total{job="pusher-metrics",journey="pusher_session"}[$__range]) or increase(omi_journey_accepted_total{job="backend-listen-metrics",journey="capture_finalization"}[$__range])) > 0)) or (0 * sum((increase(omi_journey_accepted_total{job="cloud-run-application-metrics",journey="chat_response"}[$__range]) or increase(omi_journey_accepted_total{job="pusher-metrics",journey="pusher_session"}[$__range]) or increase(omi_journey_accepted_total{job="backend-listen-metrics",journey="capture_finalization"}[$__range]))))

panels.description: Wall-clock duration (finished_at - started_at) at first durable completed persist. Live / desktop / import / integration are scraped today (backend-listen, pusher, Cloud Run backend + desktop-backend). Sync is emitted from Cloud Run backend-sync, which Prometheus does not scrape — that series is empty until the exporter allowlist grows; use the Cloud Logging panel beside this graph. A 09-19-shaped live incident is a p50 collapse toward tens of seconds. Healthy sync first chunks are ~60s, so sync p50 dropping toward ~11s is the fragment tell, not the <2min share.

panels.description: Sync intake created vs merged, read from Cloud Logging of backend-sync `omi_sync_intake outcome=created|merged`. Same query as alert omi-sync-intake-fragmented. A 09-19-shaped day is created share approaching 1.0 (one conversation per WAL chunk). Grafana log volume in this panel is the graph; the rows are the raw lines.

panels.description: Rolling one-hour share of all relevance decisions that ended in discard for backend, backend-sync, backend-sync-backfill, and backend-integration, split by service and trigger. options.content: **Rates and deltas, not levels.** This row tracks subscription *events* (created, cancellation requested/reverted, ended, payment failed) as they happen. It does not show absolute MRR/ARR or active-subscription counts — those levels live on the **[Omi TV](https://admin.omi.me/dashboard)** board (see the dashboard links menu), sourced live from Stripe. `cancellation_requested` is the leading indicator — the moment a user decided to leave. `ended` is lagging, up to a month later. `payment_failed` is involuntary churn, operationally distinct from voluntary cancellation. Counts are webhook deliveries, which Stripe may retry — this is an operational trend signal, not billing-grade numbers. Stripe (via the Omi TV board) remains source of truth.

panels.description: All subscription lifecycle events by type. Placed directly under Feature health so lifecycle shifts can be read against the same window as journey/gateway/capture health above. panels.description: Separates voluntary churn (ended after a cancellation request) from involuntary churn (payment_failed / payment_disputed). Different problems, different owners. Counts are webhook deliveries, which Stripe may retry — this is an operational trend signal, not billing-grade numbers. Stripe (via the Omi TV board) remains source of truth. `reason` is Stripe cancellation_details.reason and is only ever populated on `ended`; `payment_failed` is involuntary by construction and always carries reason="none".
